top_news.title: US sanctions three Lebanese individuals, entities over alleged financial links to Hezbollah
top_news.summary: The United States on Wednesday (local time) imposed sanctions on three Lebanese individuals and three entities, including a Hezbollah-affiliated charity and a Lebanon- and Trkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network, accusing them of facilitating the group's activities and transferring funds on its behalf, the US Department of the Treasury said. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the action was aimed at countering Iran's attempts to exert influence in the region through Hezbollah. "The Iranian regime's attempts to infringe on Lebanon's sovereignty through terror proxies like Hezbollah will not be tolerated. The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran's attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies," Bessent said in a post on X. In a press release, the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said it had designated the Wa Ta'awanu Association, a Lebanon-based charity accused of providing cover for Hezbollah's activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. It also designated members of a gold and cash smuggling network allegedly operated by Hezbollah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). According to the Treasury Department, the action exposes Hezbollah's alleged exploitation of civilian charitable organisations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance. It also seeks to increase pressure on the group's illicit financing networks as Hezbollah faces growing calls and international pressure to disarm. The Treasury Department identified Wa Ta'awanu as a Hezbollah-affiliated charity based in Lebanon that provides emergency relief services in southern Lebanon while allegedly channelling funds from outside donors towards the group's activities. It said that in July 2026, under the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure them and ensure they were free from Hezbollah fighters and weapons. However, according to the department, Wa Ta'awanu provides a pretext for Hezbollah's militant activities in the pilot zones, thereby preventing disarmament and obstructing Lebanese government efforts to secure the areas. The department identified Afif Abdel Rida Chouman as the founder of Wa Ta'awanu, alleging that he leads the charity and coordinates its activities at Hezbollah's direction. Wa Ta'awanu and Chouman were designated for allegedly materially assisting, sponsoring or providing financial, material or technological support, or goods and services, to or in support of Hezbollah. The US Treasury also targeted a gold and cash smuggling network allegedly used by Hezbollah to transfer funds from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon. According to the department, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen transferred significant amounts of money from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hezbollah in coordination with the group's financial officials. Hassan Khechen owns Lebanon-based Gold Global Company, which he allegedly uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hezbollah. The network also employs couriers to move cash across international borders. The department said Ibrahim Khechen was also involved in the group's alleged money-smuggling network and had links to a related courier who was arrested at Beirut airport in February 2025 with USD 2.5 million in his hand luggage. It further identified Trkiye-based Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), which it described as Hezbollah-affiliated and controlled by Hassan Khechen. The company allegedly assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen were designated for allegedly providing financial, material or technological support, or goods and services, to Hezbollah. Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold were designated for being owned, controlled or directed by Hassan Khechen, or acting on his behalf. The Treasury Department said the action was taken under the United States' counterterrorism authority, Executive Order 13224, as amended. It noted that the US Department of State designated Hezbollah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist on October 31, 2001, under the same executive order, citing the group's alleged involvement in acts of terrorism threatening US nationals and national security, foreign policy or economic interests. Hezbollah was earlier designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organisation on October 8, 1997, under Section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. The Treasury Department also said OFAC designated Hezbollah under Executive Order 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026, for being owned, controlled or directed by, or acting on behalf of, the IRGC-QF. Following the latest designations, all property and interests in property belonging to the designated individuals and entities that are located in the United States or are in the possession or control of US persons will be blocked and must be reported to OFAC. The restrictions also apply to entities that are directly or indirectly owned, individually or collectively, 50 per cent or more by one or more blocked persons. Unless authorised through a general or specific licence issued by OFAC, or exempt, US persons and entities are generally prohibited from conducting transactions involving the property or interests of designated persons within or transiting through the United States. The department warned that violations of US sanctions could result in civil or criminal penalties for both US and foreign individuals and entities. OFAC may also impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis. It further cautioned that financial institutions and other persons could face sanctions exposure for engaging in certain transactions involving designated individuals or entities. The prohibitions include providing funds, goods or services to designated persons, as well as receiving such contributions from them. Non-US persons are also prohibited from knowingly or unknowingly causing US persons to violate sanctions or engaging in activities intended to evade them. Additionally, foreign financial institutions that knowingly conduct or facilitate significant transactions on behalf of individuals designated under the relevant authority could face secondary sanctions. OFAC has the power to prohibit or impose strict conditions on such institutions opening or maintaining correspondent or payable-through accounts in the United States. The department said individuals in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's whistleblower incentive programme may be eligible for monetary awards if their information leads to a successful enforcement action resulting in penalties exceeding USD 1 million. It added that sanctions are intended to bring about positive changes in behaviour and that decisions to remove individuals or entities from the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List would be assessed in accordance with relevant laws, the broader geopolitical situation and US national security and foreign policy priorities. OFAC also provides a process for individuals and entities seeking removal from its sanctions lists, including the SDN List, the department said. (ANI)

articles.title: US sanctions three Lebanese individuals, entities over alleged financial links to Hezbollah
articles.summary: The United States on Wednesday (local time) imposed sanctions on three Lebanese individuals and three entities, including a Hezbollah-affiliated charity and a Lebanon- and Trkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network, accusing them of facilitating the group's activities and transferring funds on its behalf, the US Department of the Treasury said. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the action was aimed at countering Iran's attempts to exert influence in the region through Hezbollah. "The Iranian regime's attempts to infringe on Lebanon's sovereignty through terror proxies like Hezbollah will not be tolerated. The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran's attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies," Bessent said in a post on X. In a press release, the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said it had designated the Wa Ta'awanu Association, a Lebanon-based charity accused of providing cover for Hezbollah's activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. It also designated members of a gold and cash smuggling network allegedly operated by Hezbollah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). According to the Treasury Department, the action exposes Hezbollah's alleged exploitation of civilian charitable organisations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance. It also seeks to increase pressure on the group's illicit financing networks as Hezbollah faces growing calls and international pressure to disarm. The Treasury Department identified Wa Ta'awanu as a Hezbollah-affiliated charity based in Lebanon that provides emergency relief services in southern Lebanon while allegedly channelling funds from outside donors towards the group's activities. It said that in July 2026, under the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure them and ensure they were free from Hezbollah fighters and weapons. However, according to the department, Wa Ta'awanu provides a pretext for Hezbollah's militant activities in the pilot zones, thereby preventing disarmament and obstructing Lebanese government efforts to secure the areas. The department identified Afif Abdel Rida Chouman as the founder of Wa Ta'awanu, alleging that he leads the charity and coordinates its activities at Hezbollah's direction. Wa Ta'awanu and Chouman were designated for allegedly materially assisting, sponsoring or providing financial, material or technological support, or goods and services, to or in support of Hezbollah. The US Treasury also targeted a gold and cash smuggling network allegedly used by Hezbollah to transfer funds from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon. According to the department, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen transferred significant amounts of money from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hezbollah in coordination with the group's financial officials. Hassan Khechen owns Lebanon-based Gold Global Company, which he allegedly uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hezbollah. The network also employs couriers to move cash across international borders. The department said Ibrahim Khechen was also involved in the group's alleged money-smuggling network and had links to a related courier who was arrested at Beirut airport in February 2025 with USD 2.5 million in his hand luggage. It further identified Trkiye-based Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), which it described as Hezbollah-affiliated and controlled by Hassan Khechen. The company allegedly assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen were designated for allegedly providing financial, material or technological support, or goods and services, to Hezbollah. Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold were designated for being owned, controlled or directed by Hassan Khechen, or acting on his behalf. The Treasury Department said the action was taken under the United States' counterterrorism authority, Executive Order 13224, as amended. It noted that the US Department of State designated Hezbollah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist on October 31, 2001, under the same executive order, citing the group's alleged involvement in acts of terrorism threatening US nationals and national security, foreign policy or economic interests. Hezbollah was earlier designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organisation on October 8, 1997, under Section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. The Treasury Department also said OFAC designated Hezbollah under Executive Order 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026, for being owned, controlled or directed by, or acting on behalf of, the IRGC-QF. Following the latest designations, all property and interests in property belonging to the designated individuals and entities that are located in the United States or are in the possession or control of US persons will be blocked and must be reported to OFAC. The restrictions also apply to entities that are directly or indirectly owned, individually or collectively, 50 per cent or more by one or more blocked persons. Unless authorised through a general or specific licence issued by OFAC, or exempt, US persons and entities are generally prohibited from conducting transactions involving the property or interests of designated persons within or transiting through the United States. The department warned that violations of US sanctions could result in civil or criminal penalties for both US and foreign individuals and entities. OFAC may also impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis. It further cautioned that financial institutions and other persons could face sanctions exposure for engaging in certain transactions involving designated individuals or entities. The prohibitions include providing funds, goods or services to designated persons, as well as receiving such contributions from them. Non-US persons are also prohibited from knowingly or unknowingly causing US persons to violate sanctions or engaging in activities intended to evade them. Additionally, foreign financial institutions that knowingly conduct or facilitate significant transactions on behalf of individuals designated under the relevant authority could face secondary sanctions. OFAC has the power to prohibit or impose strict conditions on such institutions opening or maintaining correspondent or payable-through accounts in the United States. The department said individuals in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network's whistleblower incentive programme may be eligible for monetary awards if their information leads to a successful enforcement action resulting in penalties exceeding USD 1 million. It added that sanctions are intended to bring about positive changes in behaviour and that decisions to remove individuals or entities from the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List would be assessed in accordance with relevant laws, the broader geopolitical situation and US national security and foreign policy priorities. OFAC also provides a process for individuals and entities seeking removal from its sanctions lists, including the SDN List, the department said. (ANI)
